paragraphs.text: City beekeeping grew quickly after 2010, and some capitals now have more hives per square kilometre than the countryside around them. Rooftops of hotels and schools hold many of them.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Ecologists are uneasy. Honeybees are livestock, and a dense population of them takes nectar that wild bees and hoverflies need, especially in late summer when flowers are few.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The answer is not fewer hives alone. Cities that planted flowering strips along roads and left road verges uncut found that both honeybees and wild insects did better.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Schools that keep hives report a different gain. Pupils who look after bees learn where food comes from, and teachers use the hive in lessons from biology to mathematics.
paragraphs.label: D
